Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking our team through Redwood last week. We're moving through the security/compliance section of Skyline's vendor RFP and have a few targeted requests related to identity & access management. Would you please provide: 1) an answered questionnaire for SAML/OIDC/SCIM (we need details on SP vs IdP flows, required attributes, and SCIM support for groups), 2) description of RBAC model and how admin delegation (scoped admins) works, and 3) any artifacts you can share (SAML metadata, example SCIM schema, roles matrix).

Could we get this by EOD Wednesday (Nov 5)? Our procurement team is coordinating contract language so anything that mentions retention/audit windows would be helpful.

Attaching the RFP section for context (Skyline_RFP_IAM_v2.pdf) — please reference question numbers when you reply.

Subject: Re: RFP Q: Admin delegation, SSO & SCIM capabilities

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a completed workbook (redwood_saml_scim_answers_v1.xlsx) that maps Skyline_RFP_IAM_v2.pdf question numbers to our responses. I've summarized the high-level points inline below and attached a small provisioning diagram (scim_provisioning_flow.png).

Summary highlights (quick reference):
- SAML & OIDC: Redwood supports both SAML 2.0 (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated) and OIDC (Auth code + PKCE for browser apps). We provide SP metadata XML and OIDC discovery endpoints. Required attributes: email (primary), sub/uid, given_name, family_name. Optional: groups, department. SAML assertions can carry attribute mappings configurable per-tenant.
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 for user and group provisioning, including support for incremental (PATCH) and bulk endpoints. Group provisioning is supported (members array), and we expose schema extension points for custom attributes. Throttling: reasonable default rate limits with burst allowance; we include retry guidance in the workbook.
- RBAC & Admin delegation: Redwood's model is role-based with hierarchy. Tenant-level roles (Admin, Security Admin, Application Admin, Viewer) can be scoped to specific projects/environments. Scoped admins can be limited to a subset of groups or resources. Admin permissions are expressed as fine-grained actions (identity:manage_users, identity:manage_groups, infra:deploy_models, billing:view). We include a sample permissions matrix in the workbook (sheet: roles_matrix).
- Audit & retention: Audit logs capture admin actions, auth events, and provisioning activity. Standard retention for audit logs is 365 days for Hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we offer configurable retention up to 7 years via contract. Immutable export available for compliance reviews.
- Session & token controls: SSO sessions support configurable session TTLs and SSO token expiration. We support enforced MFA at IdP level and can integrate with SCIM-provisioned MFA attributes if needed.

Attachments included:
- redwood_saml_scim_answers_v1.xlsx (workbook with Q->A mapping, SAML metadata examples, SCIM schema examples, roles matrix)
- scim_provisioning_flow.png (diagram)

Links:
- Live OIDC discovery: https://api.redwood.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
- SAML SP metadata (example): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1SPMetadataExample

If you'd like, I can set up a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow morning to step through the workbook and the admin delegation demo.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Product Manager, Security & Identity
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@skylineit.com, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP Q: Admin delegation, SSO & SCIM capabilities

Monica — thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook. A couple quick clarifications before we close this section with procurement:

1) Scoped admins: can scoped admin roles be limited to a single customer tenant and enforced purely inside Redwood (i.e., without creating separate accounts in the IdP)? We need assurance that delegated admins cannot escalate to full org-level admin by default.
2) Retention: for Hosted customers you list 365 days. For our procurement language we want a 2-year default with the option to extend via contract. Can Redwood commit to a contractual minimum of 2 years for Hosted or provide a commercial add-on?

If you can reply to those two points I can mark the RFP item as satisfied. Otherwise we'd like to schedule the walkthrough.

Best,
Elena
